## General outline for weeks 2 -- 5

- Week 2: Principles of data visualisation
- Week 3: Grammar of graphics; aesthetics and attributes
- Week 4: Major visualisation tools
- Week 5: Customising visualisations (scales, themes, and labels)


## What is data visualisation?

- Graphical representation of data
- Graphical data analysis 
- What do we want to know?
- What do we want to communicate?
- What do people take away from your visualisation?
- Exploratory plots (for small specialist audience)
- Explanatory plots: inform and persuade wider audience


## Exploring data

```{r eval = F}
d_spellname <- read_csv("data/spellname.csv")
glimpse(d_spellname)
```

## Building up a plot

```{r}
d_vocab <- summarise(d_spellname, 
                      rt = mean(rt),
                      .by = c(ppt_id, ppt_vocab, modality)) 
glimpse(d_vocab)
```

## Building up a plot

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ggplot(data = d_vocab, 
       mapping = aes(x = ppt_vocab, 
                     y = rt, 
                     colour = modality,
                     linetype = modality))  +
  geom_point(alpha = .25) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = T, fullrange = TRUE) +
  ggthemes::theme_clean() +
  ggthemes::scale_color_colorblind() +
  labs(y = "Average reaction time (in msecs)", 
       x = "Vocabulary score",
       colour = "Response modality",
       linetype = "Response modality") +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.justification = "right",
        axis.title = element_text(hjust = 0))
```

## Explanatory plot

```{r, echo = FALSE, results=TRUE, out.width="70%"}
ggplot(data = d_vocab, 
       mapping = aes(x = ppt_vocab, 
                     y = rt,

  geom_point(alpha = .25) +

  stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = T, fullrange = TRUE) +

       colour = "Response modality",

```

## Why data visualisation? | "[data visualization] forces us to notice what we never expected to see." [@tukey1977exploratory]

- exploring structures in the data 
- relationship between variables
- distribution of data
- develop an understanding of patterns (beyond means and SDs)
- selecting appropriate stats
- prevent wrong conclusions about data / theory






## Anscombe's quartet | @anscombe1973graphs and @tufte1989


```{r echo = F, results="asis"}
anscombe <- pivot_longer(data = datasets::anscombe, 
             cols = everything(),
             names_to = c(".value", "Set"),
             names_pattern = "(.)(.)") 

ac_tab <- anscombe %>%
  nest(c(x,y)) %>%
  mutate(x_mean = map(data, ~mean(.$x)),
         x_sd = map(data, ~sd(.$x)),
         y_mean = map(data, ~mean(.$y)),
         y_sd = map(data, ~sd(.$y)),
         model = map(data, ~lm(y ~ x, data = .)),
         intercept = map(model, ~coef(.)[1]),
         slope = map(model, ~coef(.)[2]),
         cor = map(data, ~cor(.$y, .$x))) %>% 
  select(-data, -model) %>% 
  unnest(-Set) %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 2)) %>% 
  select(Set, starts_with("x"), starts_with("y"), Correlation = cor, Intercept = intercept, Slope = slope) 

ac_tab %>%
  kable("html", align = rep("c",3), 
        col.names = c("Data set", "Mean", "SD", "Mean", "SD", "Correlation", "Intercept", "Slope")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "responsive"), 
                font_size = 18, full_width = T) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" ", "x" = 2, "y" = 2, "y ~ x" = 3))
```


## Anscombe's quartet 

```{r echo = F, out.width="75%"}
anscombe %>% 
  rename(`Data set` = Set) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y = y, x = x)) +
  facet_wrap(~`Data set`, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 17)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 20)) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = T, fullrange = T, colour = "red") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold"))
```


## Anscombe's quartet 

```{r echo = F, out.width="75%"}
anscombe %>% rename(`Data set` = Set) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y = y, x = x)) +
  facet_wrap(~`Data set`, labeller = label_both) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = T, fullrange = T, colour = "red", size = .5) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 17)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 20)) +

  theme(strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold"))
```

## Principles of data visualisation

- No "one fits all" method
- Some methods are more informative than others
- Maximise what we can learn from data
- Going beyond summary statistics
- Descriptive summary statistics may conceal / obscure important patterns but minimise what we want to communicate
- Visualisation helps us to understand patterns, structures, relationships
- Prevent wrong conclusions about data / theory

## Principles of data visualisation {.columns-2}


@hartwig1979exploratory:

- *Skepticism:* any visualization might obscure or misrepresent data
- *Openness:* there might be patterns and structures that we were not expecting


@tufte1983visual:

- Above all else show the data
- Avoid distorting what the data have to say
- Present many numbers in a small space
- Encourage the eye to compare different pieces of data
- Reveal data at several levels of detail, from broad overview to fine structures


## Principles of data visualisation {.columns-2}

Edward Tufte's principles emphasise clarity, precision, and efficiency in the visual display of information. Tufte's principles guide us to create visualizations that are:

- Clear
- Honest
- Efficient
- Insightful

## Principles of data visualisation {.smaller .columns-2}

**Principle 1:** Show the Data

- Focus on the data itself
- Avoid unnecessary decoration
- Let the data tell the story


**Principle 2:** Maximize Data-Ink Ratio

- Minimize non-essential elements
- Every visual element should serve a purpose


**Principle 3:** Avoid Chartjunk

- Eliminate decorative elements that obscure the message
- Simplicity and clarity are key

\columnbreak

```{r echo = F, fig.width=5.5}
d_vocab %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = ppt_vocab, y = rt, label = ppt_vocab)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text() +
  stat_smooth(aes(colour = modality, linetype = modality, size = modality, label = modality), method = "lm") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_line(colour = "black"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 5)) +
  labs(caption = "Numbers indicate ppt_vocab",
       title = "Why is this plot terrible?",
       y = "")

```



## Principles of data visualisation {.smaller .columns-2}

**Principle 1:** Show the Data

- Focus on the data itself
- Avoid unnecessary decoration
- Let the data tell the story


**Principle 2:** Maximize Data-Ink Ratio

- Minimize non-essential elements
- Every visual element should serve a purpose


**Principle 3:** Avoid Chartjunk

- Eliminate decorative elements that obscure the message
- Simplicity and clarity are key

\columnbreak

```{r echo = F, fig.width=5.5, echo = F}
d_vocab %>% 
  mutate(across(modality, ~factor(., levels = c("writing", "speech"), ordered = T))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = ppt_vocab, y = rt, colour = modality)) +
  geom_point() +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_tufte() +
  labs(title = "Same but better",
       y = "reaction time",
       x = "vocabulary scores") +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.justification = "right")

```


## Principles of data visualisation {.smaller .columns-2}

**Principle 4:** Use Small Multiples

- Repeat charts across categories for comparison
- Supports pattern recognition

**Principle 5:** Encourage Visual Comparisons

- Design graphics to make comparisons easy
- Align scales and axes

```{r fig.width=5.5, echo = F}
d_vocab %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = modality, y = rt)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(subtitle = "Good")


```


## Principles of data visualisation {.smaller .columns-2}

**Principle 4:** Use Small Multiples

- Repeat charts across categories for comparison

```{r fig.width=5.5, echo = F}
  geom_boxplot() +
```

**Principle 4:** Use Small Multiples

- Repeat charts across categories for comparison
- Supports pattern recognition

- Design graphics to make comparisons easy
- Align scales and axes


## Principles of data visualisation {.smaller .columns-2}




**Principle 6:** Integrate Words, Numbers, and Images

- Labels should be clear and close to the data
- Avoid legends that require back-and-forth viewing



```{r fig.width=5.5, fig.height=6, echo = F}
p1 <- d_vocab %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = modality, y = rt, colour = modality)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs()

p2 <- d_vocab %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = rt, colour = modality)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "") +
  theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

p1 / p2 + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```


## Principles of data visualisation {.smaller .columns-2}


**Principle 7:** Content Over Decoration

- Focus on substance, not style
- The story should come from the data


```{r fig.width=5.5, fig.height=6, echo = F}
# Overdecorated boxplot
ggplot(d_vocab, aes(x = modality, y = rt, fill = modality)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "green", size = 1.5, outlier.colour = "red") +
  theme_dark() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "orange", size = 1),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "lightblue"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", color = "red")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Fancy Boxplot!",
    fill = "output modality\nused by the participants",
    x = "Two levels of response modality",
    y = "reaction time measure recorded from picture onset to\nresponse onset"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("magenta", "cyan", "yellow"))
```

## Principles of data visualisation {.smaller .columns-2}

**Principle 8:** Use Multivariate Displays

- Show multiple variables when appropriate
- Balance complexity with readability

**Principle 9:** Avoid Distorting the Data

- Maintain proportionality and scale
- Avoid misleading visuals



## Principles of data visualisation

- Clarity: Avoid clutter; make the message obvious
- Accuracy: Represent data truthfully
- Efficiency: Use the right chart for the right data
- Consistency: Use consistent scales, colors, and labels
- Accessibility: Consider colorblind-friendly palettes and readable fonts

## Examples of unfortunate data visualisations?

```{r}
# Sample dataset
set.seed(123)
data <- data.frame(
  category = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 10),
  value = c(rnorm(10, 10, 2), rnorm(10, 15, 2), rnorm(10, 20, 2))
)

```

```{r}
# Principle 1: Show the Data
ggplot(data, aes(x = category, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ggtitle("Good: Shows the Data Clearly")
```


```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = category, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "darkblue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey")) +
  ggtitle("Bad: Distracting Elements")

```



```{r}
# Principle 2: Maximize Data-Ink Ratio
ggplot(data, aes(x = category, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_void() +
  ggtitle("Good: High Data-Ink Ratio")

```



```{r}
# Principle 3: Avoid Chartjunk
ggplot(data, aes(x = category, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 25, label = "Look here!", color = "red", size = 6) +
  ggtitle("Bad: Unnecessary Annotation")
```
